plain.text:
Absolutely! You're in luck—there are several existing browser extensions and tools that let you export your ChatGPT conversation right from your browser window. Here's a roundup of the best options and how they work:
Extensions Available Right Now
1. ExportGPT: Export ChatGPT Conversation (Chrome)
Adds a sidebar with one-click buttons to export your chat in formats like Markdown, PDF, HTML, Excel, and more.
Lets you preview, modify, copy, or download; supports images and shared links.
Customizable export settings (e.g., hide sidebar, filename with timestamp).
2. Export ChatGPT Conversation to Notion (Chrome)
Exports your chat directly into Notion, helping you keep your conversation history neatly organized in your workspace.
3. ChatGPT Exporter (Chrome & Chromium-based browsers)
Highly rated extension (4.8/5) used by over 50,000 users.
Supports exporting in PDF, Markdown, Text, JSON, CSV, and image formats.
Allows selecting only specific chat messages, customizing file names, and preserving code blocks, tables, formulas, and other structured content.
4. ChatGPT Export (Firefox)
A lightweight Firefox add-on that cleanly exports your conversation to HTML.
Preserves formatting and code blocks, functions offline, and collects no tracking or analytics data.
What Others Say (via Reddit)
One user created a free Chrome extension to select and export either full conversations or just Q&A pairs into JSON, Markdown, or plain text.
“It lets you select Q&A pairs ... save them as JSON, Markdown, or plain text”

blocks.md: Awesome—let’s design a clean, privacy-friendly Firefox add-on that can export the currently open ChatGPT conversation exactly how you want. Below is a tight product/tech spec plus a working MV3 skeleton you can extend.

Goal: One-click export of the chat currently visible at chat.openai.com into Markdown, HTML, JSON, or PDF—without sending data anywhere.

Core features

items: Detect and extract the full conversation in the active tab (supports long chats with lazy-loaded messages).

Preserve:


speaker role (You / ChatGPT / system),


timestamps (when available),


code blocks (+ language),


inline images (embed as data URLs),


math/LaTeX blocks,


tables and lists,


message citations/footnotes text.

Export formats:


Markdown (.md) — default


HTML (.html) — styled, print-ready


JSON (.json) — structured for post-processing


PDF (.pdf) — via print-to-PDF from generated HTML

UI:


Browser action popup with buttons for each format + options.


Options page for filename template, include/exclude (images, timestamps, system prompts), theme, and “selected range only”.

Privacy:


Runs only on https://chat.openai.com/*.


No network access; no analytics.

Accessibility:


Keyboard shortcuts (e.g., Alt+Shift+E to export MD).

blocks.md: Nice-to-haves (v1.1+)

items: Obsidian-friendly frontmatter.
Notion/Google Docs handoff (download first, optional copy to clipboard).
Batch export from the left sidebar list (if open).
“Live capture” that scrolls to load and capture very long threads.

blocks.md: Manifest V3 (Firefox)

items: Action popup → sends “export” request.
Background service worker → injects content script & receives data to trigger downloads.
Content script → scrapes DOM, normalizes, serializes formats, returns payload.
Options page → stored in storage.sync.

blocks.md: Permissions
Resilience to UI changes

items:
Prefer robust selectors and fallbacks:


Try [data-testid="conversation-turn"] blocks if present.


Fallback to role/semantic cues (e.g., elements with data-message-author-role or aria labels).


Detect code blocks by pre code and keep class (language hints like language-python).

Use a DOM Harvester that:


builds a lightweight, semantic AST of each message,


never relies on fragile classnames alone,


has feature flags/matchers you can update in one place.

blocks.md: Totally possible—and smart to think about resilience up front. You can inject a real button into (or next to) ChatGPT’s per-message control strip without shipping brittle CSS or breaking every time they tweak classes. Here’s a refined spec focused on UI embedding + durability.

items:
Two display modes (auto-select at runtime):


Piggyback mode (preferred): Mount a button inside the message action row (the little hover toolbar with copy/speak/rate).


Overlay mode (fallback): Render a tiny floating button adjacent to the action row (positioned over the message container) so it feels native but doesn’t depend on internal markup.

blocks.md: If the native toolbar can’t be confidently detected, switch to Overlay mode—seamlessly.

items: A small “Export” icon button appears with the other per-message controls when you hover a message.
Clicking it opens a compact export menu (Markdown, HTML, JSON, PDF, “This message only”, “From here ↓”, “Whole thread”).
Keyboard accessible (focusable, Enter/Space activate; Esc closes menu).
Button matches theme (light/dark) and respects reduced motion.
No layout shift or jitter when the toolbar appears.
Works on the main ChatGPT site and on shared conversation pages opened at chat.openai.com.
No attempt to modify OpenAI’s menu items or hotkeys.
No persistent UI if the page is not a ChatGPT conversation.

blocks.md: Detect:

items: Start from each message root (e.g., elements with robust attributes like data-message-author-role, data-testid="conversation-turn", or article[aria-label*="assistant"|"you"]).

Within that root, locate the controls container using a set of heuristics:


Look for a region/element that contains existing buttons with predictable aria-labels (e.g., “Copy”, “Regenerate”, “Rate”, “Speak”).


Prefer role=toolbar if present.


Prefer buttons with SVG icons and aria-pressed/title patterns common to the UI.

blocks.md: Mount:

items: Create a Shadow DOM host (e.g., <span data-cgpt-export-host>), append to the end of the toolbar’s button group.

Inside the shadow root, render your button + menu.


Shadow DOM prevents ChatGPT’s CSS from restyling your UI and vice versa.


Use inherited color tokens when available; otherwise compute color from parent (e.g., getComputedStyle(toolbar).color).

blocks.md: Resilience:

items: If any heuristic fails (toolbar missing, structure changed), abort Piggyback for that message and let Overlay handle it.

blocks.text: B. Overlay Mode (adjacent to toolbar, not dependent on markup)

blocks.md: Detect anchor:

items:
Use the message bubble container as the anchor (the element that wraps the message content).
Place:

Insert an absolutely positioned tiny button in the corner where the native controls appear (e.g., bottom-right), with:


pointer-events: auto on the button


a minimal invisible offset container that follows the message’s bounding box


CSS that fades in on hover/focus of the message container to mimic native behavior
Benefits:
Stable even if ChatGPT rearranges its toolbar internals.
Looks/feels native, doesn’t overlap text, and is screen-reader labeled.
SPA route changes: Detect URL changes via history.pushState/popstate listeners and location.href polling; remount observers as needed.

MutationObserver:


Observe the main scrollable conversation area for added/removed messages or toolbar mounts.


On mutations, try (A) Piggyback; if not confident, use (B) Overlay.
Debounce: Batch mutations (e.g., 100–200ms) to avoid thrashing during streaming.
Reattachment: If ChatGPT re-renders a message, your Shadow host is removed; observer should re-inject.
Shadow DOM with a minimal reset prevents style clashes.

Colors:


Default to currentColor so the icon auto-adapts.


For backgrounds/tooltips, compute parent background or use semi-transparent backdrop to blend.
Icon: Inline SVG (no external assets) for reliability; aria-label “Export”.
Tooltip: Use aria-describedby + title for native tooltip fallback.
Button: role="button", tabindex="0", aria-label="Export conversation options".
Menu: role="menu", items role="menuitem", arrow-key navigation, focus trap, close on Esc, click-outside, or blur.
Contrast: WCAG AA for icon/label against current theme.

Scope selection:


This message only


From this message ↓ (current message + all later messages)


Whole thread (default)
Formats: Markdown / HTML / JSON / PDF.
Copy vs Download: “Copy to clipboard” items for MD/JSON; “Download” for all.
Remember last choice (stored in storage.sync, toggle in Options).

If neither Piggyback nor Overlay can mount (rare), show:


Page-level toast (“Export controls available from the toolbar icon in your browser”) and


keep the browser action popup as a universal fallback.
If PDF cannot auto-print (permissions or CSP), open a new tab with print-ready HTML and prompt the user to print/save.
Host permissions: https://chat.openai.com/*
Optional: downloads, clipboardWrite, storage
No external network requests. No analytics by default.
Strict content script origin checks before injecting.
Lightweight MutationObserver (attribute + childList).
Only one Shadow button per message.
Detach observers when tab hidden (Page Visibility API) to save work during long sessions.
Toggle: “Embed export button in ChatGPT UI” (on by default).
Toggle: “Prefer piggyback over overlay when possible.”
Default export format and scope.
Filename template (title/date).
“Show compact menu” vs “one-click export” (uses last choice).
Themes: light, dark, high-contrast (if available).
Message types: code blocks, tables, math, images, citations.
Very long threads (lazy-loaded): verify button appears on newly loaded messages after scrolling.
Shared links & read-only views.
Streaming responses (toolbar may mount late): ensure the button appears once controls exist.
Accessibility: keyboard navigation, screen reader labels.

ChatGPT DOM changes:


Mitigated by heuristic detection, ARIA/text-based anchors, Shadow DOM, and Overlay fallback.

Z-index/overlap issues:


Use local stacking context in shadow host; test across zoom levels (80–200%).

CSS adoption lag (new site styles):


Your styles isolated; icon uses currentColor to blend automatically.

blocks.md: “I’d like the export to go with those little hover buttons (rate/copy/speak). Is that possible?”

Yes. You can mount into that same toolbar (Piggyback mode) when it’s confidently identified; otherwise render a visually identical Overlay button anchored to the message. Users won’t notice the difference, and your add-on won’t break every time the site’s class names change.

If you want, we can now define the exact heuristics (list of selectors, ARIA text, and fallbacks) and the visual spec (icon, size, spacing) so implementation is plug-and-play later.

Piggyback mode (preferred): Mount a button inside the message action row (the little hover toolbar with copy/speak/rate).

If the native toolbar can’t be confidently detected, switch to Overlay mode—seamlessly.
Requirements & Acceptance Criteria
UX
A small “Export” icon button appears with the other per-message controls when you hover a message.

No layout shift or jitter when the toolbar appears.

Non-goals (v1)
No attempt to modify OpenAI’s menu items or hotkeys.
No persistent UI if the page is not a ChatGPT conversation.
UI Embedding Strategy (robustness first)
A. Piggyback Mode (inside native toolbar)
Detect:
Start from each message root (e.g., elements with robust attributes like data-message-author-role, data-testid="conversation-turn", or article[aria-label*="assistant"|"you"]).

Inside the shadow root, render your button + menu.

Use inherited color tokens when available; otherwise compute color from parent (e.g., getComputedStyle(toolbar).color).
Resilience:
If any heuristic fails (toolbar missing, structure changed), abort Piggyback for that message and let Overlay handle it.

DOM Change & Navigation Hardening

keep the browser action popup as a universal fallback.

plain.text:
Ah—that URL is on chatgpt.com, and the MVP I gave was scoped only to chat.openai.com. Two quick fixes:
1) Update the manifest to include chatgpt.com
In manifest.json, change matches/host_permissions to cover both domains:
json{
  "manifest_version": 3,
  "name": "ChatGPT Export — MVP Button",
  "version": "0.0.2",
  "description": "Injects an Export button into each ChatGPT message and echoes on click.",
  "host_permissions": [
    "https://chat.openai.com/*",
    "https://chatgpt.com/*"
  ],
  "content_scripts": [
    {
      "matches": [
        "https://chat.openai.com/*",
        "https://chatgpt.com/*"
      ],
      "js": ["content.js"],
      "run_at": "document_idle"
    }
  ]
}
2) Update the URL guard in content.js
Right now it only allows chat.openai.com. Change the check to accept either domain:
jsfunction init() {
  if (!/^https:\/\/(chat\.openai\.com|chatgpt\.com)\//.test(location.href)) return;
  // ...rest unchanged
}
3) Reload the temporary add-on
Go to about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox
Click Reload on your add-on (or “Load Temporary Add-on…” again)
Refresh your chat tab at https://chatgpt.com/c/...
That should make the button appear.
If you still don’t see it (quick checks)
Make sure you’re on a conversation page (not the home/new chat screen).
Open DevTools → Console. You should see logs after clicking the button:
[ChatGPT Export MVP] Export clicked on message ...
If nothing mounts yet, it may be a slightly different DOM on chatgpt.com. The MVP already tries multiple selectors, but you can widen the message selector quickly:
In content.js, expand getMessageSelector() (adds a safe fallback without breaking anything):
jsfunction getMessageSelector() {
  return [
    '[data-testid="conversation-turn"]',
    '[data-message-author-role]',
    'article',
    'main article',                 // extra fallback for chatgpt.com
    'div[role="article"]'           // ultra-defensive fallback
  ].join(',');

MVP scope
Show one circular Export button fixed at the bottom-right of the viewport on ChatGPT pages.
It stays put while scrolling and on long conversations.
Clicking it echoes (alert + console log). No export logic yet.
Works on both chatgpt.com and chat.openai.com.
Avoids overlapping the composer/input area by default (uses safe offsets).
Keyboard & screen-reader accessible.
Placement & layout
Position: position: fixed; right: 20px; bottom: 24px;
Use bottom: calc(24px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) to respect notches/iOS.
Size: 44×44 px (meets minimum hit target).
Shape: circular; subtle shadow.
Z-index: 2147483000 (high, but below extreme modals if they use ~2147483647).
Collision avoidance (composer):
On init and on resize, measure the chat composer bounding box.
If the button would overlap, nudge up to sit 12–16px above the composer.
Debounce recalcs to avoid thrash during window resize.
Visibility rules
Visible on: conversation pages and shared conversation pages.
Hidden on: login pages, “new chat” home if desired (optional), or any non-chat route.
Fade in/out (200 ms) on mount/unmount; respects prefers-reduced-motion.
Theming & styling
Use current theme by sampling computed styles from the body:
Background: semi-opaque surface (rgba(… , 0.85)), flips for dark/light.
Icon: uses currentColor.
Hover state: +6–8% opacity and slightly stronger shadow.
Shadow DOM for the button so site CSS can’t break it; minimal inline styles inside the shadow.
Accessibility
Button has role="button", aria-label="Export conversation", tabindex="0".
Keyboard:
Enter/Space activates (echo).
Global shortcut (optional later): Alt+Shift+E focuses/activates.
Contrast ≥ AA in both light and dark themes.
Behavior (MVP “echo”)
Click → alert("Export clicked on <domain> / <path>") and console.log with a payload:
json{ "domain": "chatgpt.com", "route": "/c/68a8…", "timestamp": "…" }
Later, we’ll swap the handler to open the export menu.
Resilience & lifecycle
No reliance on internal ChatGPT selectors.
Inject once per page load; re-check on SPA route changes:
Listen to pushState/popstate and a small location.href poll (e.g., every 500 ms) for 3s after navigation.
If URL changes between different conversation IDs, keep the button mounted; only update the echo payload.
Clean up on hard navigations (handled naturally by page reload).
Options (future, not in MVP)
Toggle “Show bottom-right button”.
Adjust offsets (right/bottom).
Reduced size / compact mode.
Acceptance criteria
The button appears in the bottom-right padding area, never covering message text for typical desktop widths.
It remains visible while scrolling and on very long threads.
On click, it alerts and logs (domain + route).
It doesn’t block typing in the composer; if the window is short or zoomed, it nudges above the composer.
Works the same on chatgpt.com and chat.openai.com.
Edge cases & handling (MVP)
Small windows / 125–150% zoom: nudge up kicks in.
Mobile / narrow widths: respect env(safe-area-inset-bottom); if overlap persists, reduce size to 40px.
High-contrast / reduced motion: inherit color; no animated transforms, only opacity fade (disabled when reduced motion).
